parameters.content:
## DryRun prep
Spots important meetings on your calendar and prepares you for them: decides if it is worth it, reads your emails with the attendees, researches the company, writes the brief, proposes the panel, saves it to the DryRun meetings table and emails you. The web app can also add a meeting by hand.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: "You decide which calendar events are worth preparing a rehearsal for. The presenter is the attendee marked "self".
Prepare for high-stakes conversations with people outside the presenter's organisation where they must persuade or perform:
sales pitches and demos, investor pitches, interviews, client reviews, partnership talks. Skip internal syncs, standups,
1:1s with colleagues, personal events and anything with no external attendee.
"why" is one specific sentence for the presenter: who is coming and what is at stake.

Event:
" + JSON.stringify($json, null, 1) }] }], generationConfig: { responseMimeType: 'application/json', responseSchema: {"type": "object", "properties": {"prepare": {"type": "boolean"}, "why": {"type": "string"}, "company": {"type": "string", "description": "The external organisation, or empty"}, "company_domain": {"type": "string", "description": "Their email or web domain, or empty"}, "kind": {"type": "string", "enum": ["sales_pitch", "investor_pitch", "interview", "client_review", "partnership", "internal", "personal", "other"]} }, "required": ["prepare", "why", "company", "company_domain", "kind"]} } }) }}

filters.q: ={{ (() => { const m = $('Read the decision').item.json; const who = m.attendees.map(a => a.email).filter(Boolean); return who.length ? '(' + who.map(e => 'from:' + e + ' OR to:' + e).join(' OR ') + ') newer_than:120d' : 'from:nobody@invalid'; })() }}

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: "Someone is about to meet {company}: a {kind} titled "{title}". Summarise what they should know, using ONLY the sources below.
In under 200 words: what the company does and its scale (from its website), then the 3 to 5 developments from the news that the
people in the meeting will most likely have on their minds (results, costs, leadership, strategy, problems), each with its date.
Do not add anything that is not in these sources. If the sources say little, say so. Plain text.

Recent news headlines (date, publisher, headline):
{news}

From their website:
{website}

From a web search (only when the news had little; facts as reported, with dates):
{web}".replace('{company}', $json.meeting.company).replace('{kind}', $json.meeting.kind).replace('{title}', $json.meeting.title).replace('{news}', $json.news.map(n => n.date + ' | ' + n.publisher + ' | ' + n.title).join('
') || 'None found.').replace('{website}', $json.website || 'Not available.').replace('{web}', $json.web_found || 'Not searched.') }] }] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ contents: [{ parts: [{ text: "You prepare a presenter for a high-stakes meeting. Write their brief, which they will rely on, so it must be accurate.

Meeting:
{meeting}

Recent emails with them:
{emails}

Research on the company (from the news, their website and a web search):
{research}

Rules:
- attendees: ONLY people named in the meeting invite or the emails above, with their real names. Never add anyone else.
  role: only if the invite or emails state it (e.g. "Rajiv from finance" -> "Finance"); otherwise an empty string. Never guess a title.
  likely_focus: what they will most likely care about or push on in this meeting, based only on the emails and research.
- practice_panel: 1 to 4 extra people for a rehearsal only, playing the roles that usually influence a decision like this at a company
  like this (e.g. CTO, procurement). Give them invented, realistic Indian names. Never use the names of real people found in the research.
  These are clearly hypothetical and are never presented as attendees.
- questions: the 5 hardest questions likely to come up. asked_by: the name of the attendee most likely to ask it, or "" if it is not
  clearly one of them. Never attribute a question to a practice_panel person. Include why it is likely and a short suggested answer.
- risks: what could lose this meeting, in short phrases, grounded in the emails and research.
- recent_news: only facts stated in the research above, each with its date. Do not add facts that are not in the research.
Answer in JSON.".replace('{meeting}', JSON.stringify($('Read the research').first().json.meeting)).replace('{emails}', $('Read the research').first().json.emails).replace('{research}', $('Read the parameters.subject: =Your brief for {{ $('Seat the panel').first().json.meeting.title }} is ready
parameters.message:
={{ (() => { const s = $('Seat the panel').first().json; const m = s.meeting; const b = s.brief; const esc = t => String(t || '').replace(/&/g, '&').replace(/ xs.length ? '
    ' + xs.join('') + '
' : '

None found.

'; const names = b.attendees.map(a => a.name); return '

' + esc(m.title) + ' with ' + esc(m.company) + '

' + esc(b.summary) + '

' + '

Who is coming

' + li(b.attendees.map(a => '
  • ' + esc(a.name) + '' + (a.role ? ' (' + esc(a.role) + ')' : '') + '. Likely focus: ' + esc(a.likely_focus) + '
    • ')) + '

    Questions likely to come up

    ' + li(b.questions.map(q => '
  • ' + esc(q.question) + (names.includes(q.asked_by) ? ' (likely from ' + esc(q.asked_by) + ')' : '') + '
    Suggested answer: ' + esc(q.suggested_answer) + '
    • ')) + '

    What could lose it

    ' + li(b.risks.map(r => '
  • ' + esc(r) + '
    • ')) + '

    Recent news about ' + esc(m.company) + '

    ' + li(b.company.recent_news.map(n => '
  • ' + esc(n.date) + ': ' + esc(n.text) + '
    • ')) + '

    Sources: ' + b.sources.map(x => '' + esc(x.title || 'link') + '').join(', ') + '

    ' + '

    Open the brief and practise in DryRun. The practice panel there adds hypothetical roles to rehearse against.

    '; })() }}
